articles.title: In 1990, Nile monitors appeared in Florida, likely via the pet trade; today they threaten sea turtles, wading birds and burrowing owls in Cape Coral
articles.summary: Discover how Nile Monitor lizards, introduced through the pet trade, are endangering Florida's native species like sea turtles and burrowing owls, particularly in Cape Coral.
articles.body: Some imported animals have proved problematic, multiplying rapidly in areas where they were never intentionally released. One such problematic animal is the Nile Monitor lizard, which hails from Africa. First spotted in Florida around 1990, this species has established itself in Cape Coral and poses a threat to Florida’s native animals. This species is problematic because it can hunt on the ground, in trees and in water.How Nile Monitors became established in FloridaNile monitors (Varanus niloticus) are indigenous to sub-Saharan Africa, where they exist in various environments from the river banks to wetlands. These monitors are strong swimmers, skilled climbers and opportunistic feeders that prey on various animal species. The species has been present in the Cape Coral area of Lee County since around 1990. The Nile monitor is thought to have reached Florida through the exotic pet trade, though exactly how the animals arrived is unknown.Pet owners can introduce non-native species to the wild by releasing animals that have grown too large or too difficult to keep. A 2004 study by Kevin Enge and colleagues in Southeastern Naturalist, “Status of the Nile Monitor (Varanus niloticus) in Southwestern Florida,” describes the early stages of the population’s establishment. Between April 2001 and July 2003, the team compiled 146 sightings or captures of the lizards, mostly reported by local residents. These figures reflect the early years of the invasion. Lizards of all size classes were recorded, suggesting a reproducing population. The data also indicate that the lizards have expanded their range northwards and to nearby islands.Why Cape Coral provides suitable habitatThere are plenty of canals, waterways and residential areas in Cape Coral, which put people and animals in close contact. The waterways provide access to prey and allow them to move from one habitat to another. These lizards either dig holes themselves or use pre-existing holes for shelter and nesting. It is difficult to control them because of their adaptability to different environments, especially where developed lands meet wetlands and other natural areas. The City of Cape Coral lists Nile monitors among the large invasive lizards found locally. Its guidance on invasive lizards treats them as a wildlife issue and notes that the city traps them. These lizards can be several feet long and eat fish, reptiles, birds, small mammals and eggs. Due to a wide range of prey items, they can impact various parts of an ecosystem rather than depending on one food item.Native wildlife faces several risksThere is cause for concern due to the feeding habits of Nile monitors because they have the same diet as vulnerable native animals. These reptiles can feed on turtle eggs and hatchlings and steal eggs from bird nests. Enge and colleagues identified turtles, wading birds and burrowing owls as potentially at risk. Burrowing owls are notable in Cape Coral because it houses the largest number of these birds in Florida. Burrowing owls nest underground, so reptiles that hunt for eggs and young on the ground could prey on them. They also warned that sea turtles and wading birds could be affected if the lizards spread into nearby sensitive areas where these animals nest or forage. This does not mean Nile monitors are responsible for every decline in native species.Genetic research traces the lizards' originsIn addition, studies have been carried out to find out where the Nile monitors in Florida originated from and how their introduced populations arose. A 2016 study by Stephanie Dowell and colleagues in Royal Society Open Science, “Combining genetic and distributional approaches to sourcing introduced species: a case study on the Nile monitor (Varanus niloticus) in Florida,” looked at where Florida’s lizards came from. The researchers analysed genetic material from 25 Florida lizards and compared it with reference samples from across the species’ native range in sub-Saharan Africa.The study found that the breeding populations at Cape Coral, West Palm Beach and Homestead Air Reserve Base came from three separate introduction events. All of them originated from the southern coastal region of West Africa.Trapping aims to limit further spreadThe City of Cape Coral manages Nile monitors by trapping them. Locating and then capturing the individuals could be of assistance in managing the population of Nile monitors in the area. However, the lizards’ reproductive ability and their movement through waterways make their populations difficult to manage. Owners of exotic reptiles should understand that if these animals are released into the wild, they can harm the environment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Australia eyes Israel’s Iron Dome: Why is Canberra building a missile shield?
articles.summary: Australia is considering acquiring missile interceptors developed for Israel’s Iron Dome as part of efforts to establish an air defence system, officials
articles.body: Australia is considering acquiring missile interceptors developed for Israel’s Iron Dome as part of efforts to establish an air defence system, officials told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.Defence officials said Australia aimed to have a ground-based missile defence system in place by the early 2030s, citing lessons from rapidly changing warfare in Ukraine and the Middle East.The options under discussion include the US Patriot missile defence system and interceptor missiles developed by Israeli defence company Rafael Advanced Defence Systems for Iron Dome.The interceptors have recently been used in a new system developed for the US Marine Corps and are jointly manufactured with US company Raytheon, AFP reported.The Iron DomeIsrael’s Iron Dome is a short- to medium-range air defence system developed by Israeli defence company Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. According to Rafael, the system has recorded more than 10,000 successful interceptions since 2011, with a success rate exceeding 90 per cent. It is designed to intercept a range of aerial threats, including rockets, artillery shells, mortars, cruise missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The company says the system can operate in different weather conditions and respond to multiple incoming threats simultaneously.Iron Dome system is part of a wider family of air defence systems that includes C-Dome, its naval variant, and I-Dome, a mobile configuration. These systems are designed to protect civilian population centres, military forces, maritime assets and strategic infrastructure.According to the company, Iron Dome’s architecture can be integrated with other sensors and command-and-control systems as part of a layered air defence network. Rafael also says the United States Marine Corps selected the system to strengthen its expeditionary air defence capabilities.Truck-mounted, medium-range interceptors were tested by the US Marines in Guam in June during a regional military exercise that Australia also participated in, AFP reported.Australia does not supply weapons to Israel, and potential purchases of Israeli defence equipment have come under political scrutiny.“The government will always seek to deliver the most suitable military technology,” government minister Murray Watt told the committee when asked about the issue.Air Marshal Robert Chipman said the defence force would make recommendations to the government next year following a competitive selection process linked to the Talisman Sabre military exercise in 2027.

articles.title: ‘RSS Friends’ enters US foreign-agent register, cites concerns over portrayal of Sangh
articles.summary: A group of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) well-wishers has registered with the US Department of Justice (DoJ) as a foreign agent representing the
articles.body: A group of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) well-wishers has registered with the US Department of Justice (DoJ) as a foreign agent representing the organisation. The group, named RSS Friends, aims to expand outreach in the US and respond to information it considers inaccurate or lacking relevant context.The group registered under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) on August 27, listing the RSS at Keshavkunj, New Delhi, as its “foreign principal”. The registration document provided a Georgia address for the group.According to the filing, RSS Friends intends to undertake informational, educational, public-relations and community engagement activities, including responding to accounts of the RSS that it believes are inaccurate, incomplete or lack relevant context.“RSS Friends does not have a written employment, consulting, lobbying, public-relations, or agency agreement with RSS containing specified deliverables, compensation, or detailed operational instructions,” the group said in its filing.It cautioned, however, that the absence of a written contract should not be interpreted as meaning there is no relationship or coordination between the two organisations.“RSS Friends will disclose the actual facts relevant to its activities,” it said.The group said it may engage with journalists, media organisations, researchers, academic and policy institutions, community leaders and civil-society organisations. It also listed participation in educational, cultural, community and informational events among its proposed activities.“Consistent with its governing documents and applicable law, it may communicate with members of the public, journalists, media organisations, researchers, academic and policy institutions, community leaders, civil-society organisations, and, where appropriate, government agencies or officials,” RSS Friends said.The filing describes the RSS as an India-based volunteer and social-cultural organisation. Its board of directors comprises Rajendra Sonarikar, Jayant Pant and Devananda Gaddam.On its website, RSS Friends says its efforts are aimed at addressing what it describes as misconceptions about the organisation and their impact on the Indian diaspora, particularly Hindu Americans.“In the United States, politically motivated actors and media often misrepresent the RSS, creating negative repercussions for the Indian diaspora, particularly Hindu-Americans,” the website states.It adds, “We believe that over time, these efforts will dispel misconceptions about the RSS and, more importantly, support the integrity of the Hindu-American community.”The registration was submitted two days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s Universal Oneness Celebration at New York’s Madison Square Garden on August 29. The event was organised by the American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD) Forum, according to the filing-related reports.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Washington couple said their neighbour blocked a shared driveway, cut power to security cameras and turned off their water; an October 27 appeals court upheld the anti-harassment order protecting them
articles.summary: A long-running dispute between neighbours in Washington State has ended, at least for now, with a state appeals court backing an anti-harassment order
articles.body: A long-running dispute between neighbours in Washington State has ended, at least for now, with a state appeals court backing an anti-harassment order that protects a couple who said their neighbour blocked a shared driveway, cut electricity to their security cameras and shut off their water. The Washington Court of Appeals, Division III, upheld the protection order on October 27, according to the published decision in case number 41231-8, via Justia Law.The case is a reminder that neighbour conflicts do not always remain minor disagreements over property lines, parking or maintenance. When a pattern of conduct begins to interfere with a family’s safety, access to their home or basic utilities, the law can treat it as harassment rather than an ordinary civil quarrel. In this dispute, the appellate court concluded that the lower court had sufficient grounds to keep the protective order in place.What the couple allegedAccording to the account described in the appeals court record, the couple said the trouble began with the shared driveway outside their homes. They alleged that their neighbour blocked the driveway, making it harder for them to come and go from their property. For many households, a driveway is not simply a convenience. It can be the main route for emergency vehicles, deliveries, visitors and daily travel, so blocking it can quickly turn a property disagreement into a safety concern.The couple also said the neighbour interfered with the electricity supply to their security cameras. Security cameras are often installed to give homeowners peace of mind, especially when tensions with someone nearby are already high. If the power to those cameras is disrupted, residents may feel exposed and unable to document what is happening around their home. The court record indicates that the couple raised this alleged interference as part of their harassment claims.Perhaps most seriously, the couple alleged that their water was turned off. Access to running water is a basic household need, affecting drinking, cooking, sanitation and hygiene. An allegation that someone deliberately cut off another household’s water supply goes well beyond the kind of irritation that commonly arises between neighbours. It suggests conduct that can make a home difficult or unsafe to live in.Why the court upheld the orderThe appeals court was asked to decide whether the anti-harassment order should remain in effect. After reviewing the case, the Division III court upheld the order on October 27. The decision means the protections granted to the couple will stand, subject to the terms set by the court.Washington’s anti-harassment laws allow courts to issue protection orders when someone engages in a course of conduct directed at another person that seriously alarms, annoys, harasses or harms them, and that serves no legitimate or lawful purpose. The conduct must also be serious enough that a reasonable person would suffer substantial emotional distress, and the person seeking protection must actually experience that distress.That legal standard matters because courts do not issue these orders over every unpleasant interaction. A single argument, a misplaced rubbish bin or a disagreement about who should repair a fence will not usually meet the threshold. But when actions accumulate into a pattern that interferes with someone’s ability to live safely and peacefully in their own home, a court may find that the behaviour crosses into unlawful harassment.In this case, the alleged conduct involved access to the property, surveillance equipment and an essential utility. Taken together, those allegations painted a picture of sustained interference rather than an isolated dispute. The appeals court’s decision to uphold the order suggests it found the trial court’s assessment of the evidence and the need for protection to be sound.Why neighbour disputes can escalateNeighbour disputes often start over something small. A shared driveway can create confusion about who may park where, who is responsible for snow removal or repairs, and whether one household is blocking another’s access. Because both parties live side by side, there is no easy way to avoid contact, and small grievances can build over months or years.Disputes involving shared driveways, easements, fences, drainage, trees and boundaries are especially common because property records do not always answer every practical question. A driveway may be legally shared even if one neighbour has historically used it more often. A utility line may cross one property to serve another. Without clear communication, each side may believe the other is acting unreasonably.The danger is that frustration can lead to retaliation. Instead of resolving the underlying issue, one party may begin taking actions intended to pressure, punish or inconvenience the other. Blocking access, interfering with utilities or disabling security measures can feel like an escalation from disagreement to intimidation. Courts are particularly concerned when that conduct appears deliberate and continuing.What protection orders can doAn anti-harassment order can impose several kinds of restrictions. Depending on the facts, a court may prohibit contact, prevent a person from coming near the protected household, restrict surveillance, or order someone to stop specific conduct. The goal is not to punish the respondent through the order itself, but to prevent further harassment while the underlying issues are addressed through the proper legal channels.In earlier Washington cases, courts have upheld anti-harassment orders that barred neighbours from surveilling one another. In one Division Two case, the court affirmed an order preventing a neighbour from surveilling the people who sought protection, finding that Washington law expressly allows courts to prohibit attempts to keep a victim under surveillance.That does not mean every camera or every observation of a neighbour is illegal. People may have legitimate reasons to record activity on their own property, particularly if they are concerned about damage or safety. But when recording, monitoring or other conduct becomes part of a campaign aimed at frightening or controlling a neighbour, courts can consider it within the scope of harassment.The wider lesson for homeownersFor homeowners, the case highlights the importance of documenting problems early and seeking help before a conflict becomes dangerous. If a neighbour is blocking access to a shared driveway, repeatedly interfering with utilities or damaging security equipment, residents should keep dated records, photographs, messages and any other evidence that shows what happened and when.It is also wise to contact local authorities or a lawyer when essential services or safe access to a home are affected. A blocked driveway may require different help than a cut water line or a disabled security system, but all three can support a broader claim that a neighbour’s conduct has become more than a property disagreement.The October 27 ruling does not erase the underlying tension between the neighbours, and it does not decide every possible property-rights question that may exist between them. What it does do is confirm that the couple’s request for protection was legally justified. For them, the court’s decision provides a formal boundary and a measure of security after conduct they said made their home harder to live in.For everyone else, it offers a simple lesson: neighbours may disagree, but they cannot use access, utilities or fear as weapons. When a dispute becomes a pattern of interference, Washington courts have shown they are willing to step in.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Apple announces its first touchscreen MacBook Pro: Price in India, features, availability and other things to know
articles.summary: Apple has introduced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, featuring breakthrough tandem OLED technology.
articles.body: Apple has introduced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, featuring breakthrough tandem OLED technology. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch models, the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display introduces intuitive touch capabilities on the Mac for the first time. Featuring M5 Pro and M5 Max, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and now up to 16TB of blazing-fast storage, the new MacBook Pro delivers speed and capability for the most demanding workflows. The laptop will be available from November 6 onwards. Here’s everything you need to know about Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook ProApple MacBook Pro pricePrice of the 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Pro starts at Rs 3,49,900 and Rs 3,31,900 with education savings. The 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Pro comes with a starting price of Rs 4,09,900 and Rs 3,85,900 with education savings.The 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Max, on the other hand costs Rs 5,49,900 and Rs 5,12,900 with education savings. The 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Max comes with a starting price of Rs 5,89,900 and Rs 5,52,900 with education savings.Apple MacBook Pro availabilityThe all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is already up for pre-orders starting October 28, on apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app in 30 countries and regions, including the US. The laptop will begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers, starting Monday, November 9.Apple MacBook Pro displayAs mentioned above, the all new Apple MacBook Pro comes with a PROLED XDR display that offers tandem OLED technology. It’s all backed by advanced algorithms in the display engine that precisely control each pixel in real time, plus a meticulous manufacturing process and precise calibration of every panel for consistency from display to display.PROLED XDR offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness. Through optimisations in the tandem OLED panel and custom compensation techniques, combined with precise control of light across the display, the PROLED XDR display achieves an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The ProMotion technology on the device delivers adaptive refresh rates from as low as 10Hz for better power efficiency and up to 120Hz for fluid responsiveness for content in motion.MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time. Apple says that the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.Apple MacBook Pro features Dynamic IslandThe Dynamic Island feature is finally available on Mac with the all-new MacBook Pro. Just like on iPhone, the Dynamic Island provides a quick, intuitive way to see and interact with important information. Users can ask a question, pick up a phone call, or control music — all within easy reach. With Live Activities, users can now get timely updates at a glance, and can accept an AirDrop request or pause a song with a tap of their finger.Apple MacBook Pro designThe new MacBook Pro is thinner and significantly lighter for even better portability. The 14-inch MacBook Pro weighs half a pound less at 3 pounds (1.36 kg (approximately)., while the 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs just 4 pounds — 0.7 pounds lighter than before.Both models feature a slimmer design enabled by OLED’s more efficient display stack, with the 16-inch model nearly a millimetre thinner and the 14-inch model half a millimetre thinner.Apple MacBook Pro processorThe all-new MacBook Pro features M5 Pro and M5 Max claimed to deliver phenomenal single- and multithreaded CPU performance, along with faster unified memory. Apple says M5 Pro offers game-changing performance for scientists, engineers, software developers, and creative pros tackling intensive projects, accelerating everything from compiling code and running AI tasks to sequencing DNA and editing multiple streams of 8K ProRes video.M5 Max, on the other hand, is built for users who want to push the limits even further, including 3D VFX artists, AI developers, and film composers. With M5 Max, pros can run LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device and accelerate intense workflows across detailed visual effects, 3D animation projects, film scores, and 8K video post-production.Both M5 Pro and M5 Max feature a GPU with enhanced shader cores and a third-generation ray-tracing engine, delivering more photorealistic lighting and faster renders for 3D modelling. Dynamic Caching optimises on-chip memory to significantly increase GPU utilisation, driving huge performance boosts for apps like Blender and Unreal Engine, along with AAA games.Apple MacBook Pro audio systemThe new MacBook Pro features a six-speaker audio system that provides 50 percent deeper bass and all-new tweeters that shape sound dispersion for remarkable clarity. Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos wraps users in immersive sound for music and movies, and studio-quality mics deliver clean, clear audio for calls, recordings, and voice commands. For the first time, the laptop comes with a dedicated audio tuning for closed-lid use.Apple MacBook Pro connectivityThe new MacBook Pro includes three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. In addition to the PROLED XDR display, it supports up to three external displays with M5 Pro and up to four with M5 Max. Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 provide fast, reliable wireless connectivity, and Touch ID enables a quick, easy, and secure login experience. In addition, storage is now configurable up to 16TB.Apple MacBook Pro OSThe new MacBook Pro comes to life with macOS 27. In addition to Touch built for macOS 27, MacBook Pro includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across apps; and an expansive set of improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable.Siri AI can draw on personal context to help pros find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence by using a dedicated keyboard shortcut to get help with a specific item. Pros can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.Apple MacBook Pro batteryThe all-new Apple MacBook Pro comes with fast-charge capability. Apple says that the latest MacBook Pro can charge up to 50 percent in just 30 minutes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US midterms: FBI, ICE agents will not serve as election monitors, DOJ says
articles.summary: The US Department of Justice said FBI and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel will not serve as monitors during the November midterm
articles.body: The US Department of Justice said FBI and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel will not serve as monitors during the November midterm elections, amid concerns from civil rights groups that the Trump administration’s plans for federal election oversight could intimidate voters.In a court filing late Wednesday in a lawsuit brought by the NAACP, the Justice Department said federal election monitors would observe polling places, take notes and would not act as law enforcement personnel, reported Reuters. They would also be prohibited from carrying firearms and have been trained not to interfere with voting or violate state and local rules, the filing said.While employees of the Federal Bureau of Prisons, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) will serve as monitors, the department said neither FBI nor ICE employees would be deployed in that role.Concerns over the possible deployment of federal law enforcement officers at polling sites had grown in the run-up to the midterms. Last month, a coalition of civil rights groups led by the NAACP sued the Trump administration, seeking to prevent ICE agents and other federal law enforcement personnel from being stationed at polling locations. The groups argued that the prospect of such a deployment could intimidate voters, particularly Black, Latino and Asian communities, naturalised citizens and members of mixed-status families.Even President Donald Trump declined to rule out sending ICE officers or National Guard personnel to polling locations. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had said ICE would not patrol polling sites but could respond if there was a threat at a location or agents needed to serve a warrant.The Trump administration has also stepped up scrutiny of voter registration records, pressing states for voter data and arguing that stricter oversight is necessary to maintain confidence in elections. Some officials told Reuters this month that they were preparing for potential federal interference in the midterms.The Justice Department’s filing addresses the role of election monitors, while the broader legal challenges also contest the administration’s increased scrutiny of voter rolls. The groups argue that the presence, or threat of deployment, of federal officers could amount to voter intimidation and violate protections under federal voting-rights law.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump’s DHS hit by data breach as hackers expose records of 41,000 employees
articles.summary: More than 41,000 employees and contractors of the US department of homeland security (DHS), including thousands of immigration and border enforcement
articles.body: More than 41,000 employees and contractors of the US department of homeland security (DHS), including thousands of immigration and border enforcement personnel, have had their work details exposed in a major data leak amid growing protests and criticism over President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown.The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves.The leaked information includes names, work addresses, phone numbers and job descriptions of personnel working across several agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), a BBC report reveals.The leaked records were published in a searchable online database called “Icepick” on Wednesday. The activist group department of peace said it accessed the information through a single sign-on service used by DHS employees, while cybersecurity researcher Maia Arson Crimew and the nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets helped make the data public.DHS acknowledges potential breachA DHS spokesperson said the department was “aware of a potential breach” and was working to address the situation. The spokesperson added that the agency takes security threats against its employees and officers seriously and would provide further updates when more information became available.According to the leaked data, more than 21,000 personnel listed work for CBP, while nearly 6,600 are associated with ICE. Other records reportedly cover employees of homeland security investigations, the federal protective service and the cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency.The groups behind the disclosure, however, said the database was not intended to be a comprehensive directory of all DHS employees. Rather the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability", according to Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Marcelle Flowers, 62, feared AI would take jobs until two young founders solved a $5,000-a-month problem at her plumbing business and made her COO of a startup that raised $52 million
articles.summary: At 62, Marcelle Flowers had spent decades building her career in the plumbing industry when two young entrepreneurs arrived at her Sacramento business
articles.body: At 62, Marcelle Flowers had spent decades building her career in the plumbing industry when two young entrepreneurs arrived at her Sacramento business with an idea for using artificial intelligence. Initially sceptical of the technology, Flowers agreed to test their automated appointment reminder system after recognising a problem it could solve. The meeting soon developed into a working partnership that helped shape Broccoli AI, a startup founded by engineers Jain and Ketkar. Flowers became the company's first chief operating officer, bringing practical industry experience to a business that has since raised $52 million in venture funding and expanded to more than 1,500 customers, as reported by Fortune.From BITS Pilani to Broccoli AI: How Jain and Ketkar found a new startup opportunityJain and Ketkar had already spent several years trying to establish themselves as entrepreneurs before they began visiting plumbing, heating and electrical contractors in Northern California. According to Fortune reports, the pair met at BITS Pilani in India in 2016 and started working on businesses together the following year. Their earlier ventures included a delivery service for university campuses and an interview preparation programme.After joining Y Combinator, they developed an application programming interface for electric vehicles and moved to London to pursue the idea. They secured eight customers over two years, but the business struggled to grow despite receiving seed funding. The founders moved to San Francisco in January 2024, looking for a different direction.That spring, they began visiting contractors in person, travelling through the Bay Area and into Stockton, Lodi, Modesto and Sacramento. They eventually called on roughly 140 businesses. The founders wanted to understand how smaller trade businesses operated, rather than designing a product from the perspective of a large corporation. They were also looking for an experienced operator who could help them turn what they heard into something useful.How a $5,000 monthly answering service bill helped shape Broccoli AIFlowers was initially sceptical when her employees told her that two young men were waiting at the counter. She assumed they might be selling fundraising chocolates and was prepared to give them only a few minutes of her time.At 62, she had little enthusiasm for the idea of introducing AI into a business built around human relationships. The founders, meanwhile, had arrived with a simple automated telephone call designed to remind customers about upcoming appointments.The demonstration caught her attention because it addressed a problem she already had. The employee responsible for making those reminder calls had left Armstrong Plumbing, and Flowers had not found a replacement.She agreed to try the product. Within two days, Jain and Ketkar had adapted it using the scripts she supplied. The trial soon moved beyond appointment reminders, however, when Flowers explained that her answering service was a much bigger expense.Reportedly, she was paying about $5,000 a month for the service, which entered bookings into her company's scheduling software only around a third of the time, according to her account. She wanted to know whether the founders could develop a system that handled incoming calls as well. They returned with a working version in about 10 days.Marcelle Flowers helped shape Broccoli AI’s product and public identityFor roughly three months, the founders worked from Flowers' Sacramento premises instead of spending all their time at their San Francisco office. She walked them through the daily demands of a contracting business, explaining the language, processes and customer expectations they had not encountered in their engineering careers.Word of mouth took Broccoli AI from its first customer to 10, allowing the founders to reduce their reliance on cold calls. Flowers became an adviser before taking on the role of chief operating officer.She also helped shape the company's public identity, working on its logo, colour scheme and first trade-show booth. Her contribution extended beyond business advice: she had become involved in the company's development at a point when the founders were still deciding what the product should do. Flowers later moved into an apartment in San Francisco to work with the startup.Marcelle Flowers' journey from a single mother to a successful plumbing business leaderFlowers grew up in Anaheim, California, in a family closely connected to construction. Her father was a commercial plumber whose projects included restaurants, hotels and schools. She became pregnant at 19 and raised her son as a single mother. She has described the years from her mid-teens to her mid-twenties as a period when she made decisions she later regretted. Finding her faith at 26 marked a change in direction, she told Fortune.She joined her father's company in 1995. In 2011, she established its residential service-and-repair operation, which she said grew from approximately $1 million in annual business to $8 million over seven years without outside investment, as reported by Fortune.The business suffered during the COVID-19 period. Flowers said she experienced long COVID for about nine months, while the company's performance deteriorated. She had also previously battled cancer twice, describing both diagnoses as terminal.“I literally said, you have five minutes,” recalled Flowers, now 62 years old. It was June 2024, and a deal to sell her business, Armstrong Plumbing, had fallen through months earlier. She was also “really opposed to AI.”She feared it would take her people and “take all the jobs.”What Broccoli AI does for contractorsBroccoli AI develops voice-based agents for businesses that provide plumbing, heating, ventilation, air conditioning and electrical services. The software can answer incoming calls, schedule jobs through existing systems, contact customers about outstanding estimates and manage service-membership renewals.These tasks may appear routine, but they can create substantial pressure for small companies. Calls continue to arrive after office staff have left for the day, technicians need to follow up on estimates, and owners must keep track of appointments while managing the work itself.The company says its technology can perform work equivalent to roughly 30% of a typical contractor's office staff. articles.body: BHOPAL: Two sisters, one of whom was eight months pregnant, allegedly jumped into wells with their four children in two separate incidents in Madhya Pradesh’s Shivpuri district on Wednesday, leaving all six dead.Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, Sita Rawat, 40, was found dead with her three children — Rakhi, 14, Priyanka, 11, and Shlok, 6 — in a well in Khonkar village, under Kolaras police station limits.Police are investigating the two incidents separately and are yet to establish the reasons behind the deaths.Anjali’s three daughters were also present when she allegedly jumped into the well with her son. Relatives rushed to the spot and pulled Anjali and Prashant out of the well, but both had died. Anjali’s unborn child also died.According to family members, Anjali’s husband, Dharmveer Singh Rawat, died in a road accident around one-and-a-half months ago. Police are examining the circumstances surrounding the incident.Sita, a resident of Sesai village, had gone to a field in Khonkar village with her three children. When they had not returned home by around 6pm, relatives began searching for them.They found slippers near a well and spotted a child’s body inside, following which they alerted the police. Kolaras police retrieved the bodies of Sita and her three children by around 11pm.Family members said the sisters were close and frequently spoke to each other over the phone. articles.title: Decoys, secret jet and Trump's help: How Bolsonaro pulled off his escape from Brazil to US
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro’s journey from Brazil to the United States involved decoy cars, a cross-border transfer through Argentina and Ecuador, and assistance
articles.body: Flávio Bolsonaro’s journey from Brazil to the United States involved decoy cars, a cross-border transfer through Argentina and Ecuador, and assistance from allies of US President Donald Trump.The defeated Brazilian presidential candidate and his family reached Miami on Wednesday after an operation coordinated by a small circle of US officials and aides to Argentina president Javier Milei, The Wall Street Journal reported.Flávio Bolsonaro’s departure came after he lost Brazil’s presidential runoff election to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Brazil’s Supreme Court had ordered him to surrender his passports within 24 hours as part of a money-laundering investigation and barred him from leaving the country. Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing.Four cars, decoy and a carefully concealed departureAfter Bolsonaro stepped off the plane in Miami on Wednesday morning, wearing a navy polo shirt and a backpack, uniformed officers used umbrellas to shield him from cameras.According to the reports, Bolsonaro left his home in Brasília on Monday evening in a convoy of four dark vehicles. The cars split in different directions, leaving journalists and others uncertain about which one was carrying him.The report said that even some of Bolsonaro’s close allies in Washington and Brazil were initially unaware of his whereabouts. By Tuesday afternoon, however, allies were telling reporters that he had reached Florida, although he was still in Brazil at the time.Also Read| 72 hours, 3 countries, 1 private jet: Flavio Bolsonaro’s wild escape to USThe operation took shape on Monday as people close to Bolsonaro grew concerned that he could face arrest, the WSJ reported. His legal troubles predated the election, but the court order restricting his travel intensified those concerns.From Argentina to Miami on a private jetBolsonaro, his wife and their two daughters travelled by road towards Argentina. According to Argentine authorities cited in the report, the family crossed the Tancredo Neves International Bridge into Puerto Iguazú at around 10:50 pm local time on Tuesday.Their vehicle was escorted by Argentine airport security police to the immigration checkpoint at Iguazú Falls International Airport. A former Argentine intelligence official told the newspaper that Santiago Caputo, a senior aide to Milei, was monitoring the operation and coordinating with Bolsonaro’s younger brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro.A private Gulfstream jet, operated by charter airline Baires Fly, was waiting at the airport. Flight-tracking data showed that the aircraft travelled to Guayaquil, Ecuador, to refuel before continuing to the United States.Bolsonaro travelled using an Italian passport. He had reportedly acquired Italian citizenship in 2023.Also Read| Why Flávio Bolsonaro fled Brazil for the US — and what happens nextThe jet landed at Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport on Wednesday morning. Officers used umbrellas to shield the family from cameras as they were escorted to a waiting vehicle.Trump’s approval and a long-running allianceThe WSJ reported that Trump personally approved the family’s entry into the US on Tuesday, after which secretary of state Marco Rubio moved to issue visas. The family was admitted under humanitarian parole, allowing them to remain in the country for one year, according to people familiar with the arrangements cited by the newspaper.Trump adviser Jason Miller helped secure the charter flight, working with Eduardo Bolsonaro. The operation marked the culmination of years of efforts by the Bolsonaro family to cultivate ties with Trump and his inner circle.In a statement from Miami, Bolsonaro referred to himself as the “leader of Brazil” and thanked Trump for welcoming him to a “land of freedoms”. He also praised Milei for his “courage” and “sense of justice”.Trump, meanwhile, said of the Bolsonaros, “I thought they were treated very unfairly.” He added: “But I won’t get involved—it was a very strange election, that’s for sure.”Bolsonaro is reportedly planning to establish a political operation in exile in the US, although it remains unclear whether the Trump administration will take further steps to intervene in Brazil’s domestic political and legal disputes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Fire at South Carolina nuclear site triggers emergency; restrictions lifted after no contamination detected
articles.summary: A fire at the Savannah River National Laboratory in US' South Carolina triggered a site-area emergency on Wednesday, disrupting road, rail and air
articles.body: A fire at the Savannah River National Laboratory in US' South Carolina triggered a site-area emergency on Wednesday, disrupting road, rail and air movement around the nuclear facility. Traffic restrictions have since been lifted after the fire was extinguished and officials confirmed that radiological surveys detected no contamination outside the site.The emergency was terminated at 9:45 pm local time on Thursday, following which site barricades were reopened and protective measures lifted, according to the SRS. Employees were asked to report for their shifts as usual.“A fire was reported at the Savannah River National Laboratory but has since been extinguished. Radiological surveys indicated no detectable levels of contamination. Highway 125 remains open at this time. SRS officials are directing response efforts and have notified the appropriate state and local government agencies,” the site said in a statement.The fire triggered restrictions on incoming traffic and affected air and rail movement in the surrounding area. Officials declared a “Site Area Emergency”, the second-highest of three emergency categories at the facility, indicating that a significant incident had occurred.The Savannah River Site is a major US government installation that once produced materials used in nuclear weapons, primarily tritium and plutonium-239. Opened in the early 1950s during the Cold War, the complex now focuses on environmental cleanup, nuclear waste management and the handling of nuclear materials, according to the US Department of Energy.The laboratory, located in the north-western part of the site, conducts experiments involving nuclear materials and processes radioactive substances. It also operates a facility that recovers radioisotopes from used nuclear fuel.Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists, said the confirmation of no contamination beyond the site was reassuring. However, he stressed the need for caution when fires occur in facilities handling radioactive materials.“If you have a fire where there is radioactive material, you need to take extreme precautions because of the potential dispersal of that material and the potential for contamination, potential for the public to be exposed,” Lyman said.While officials have confirmed that the fire is out and no detectable off-site contamination was found, the incident has renewed attention on emergency preparedness at facilities handling radioactive materials.You use AI every day. articles.body: GHAZIABAD: CCTV footage has emerged showing the sequence of events in which a woman and her gym trainer allegedly plotted an attack on her husband, who was stabbed while sleeping beside their young daughter in Ghaziabad on Monday.The footage, recorded on October 26, shows Priya leaving her house around 5.17am and driving away in her car.About three minutes later, at 5.20am, her alleged lover, Pratap Singh, a gym trainer, is seen entering the house. articles.title: A New Jersey homeowner tried to stop a neighbour's plunge pool just eight feet from a waterfront bulkhead, claiming it could worsen flooding; an October 26 appeals court upheld dismissal of the challenge
articles.summary: How close is too close when a neighbour builds a swimming pool beside a waterfront property already vulnerable to flooding?
articles.body: How close is too close when a neighbour builds a swimming pool beside a waterfront property already vulnerable to flooding? For one family in Toms River, New Jersey, the proposed installation of an in-ground plunge pool raised concerns about tidal water flowing onto their land, coastal construction rules and whether local authorities had properly issued the necessary permits. David Faloba, acting on behalf of his parents, challenged the project, arguing that the pool could worsen flooding and that the approvals did not comply with environmental requirements.On October 26, 2026, the New Jersey Superior Court's Appellate Division upheld the dismissal of Faloba's lawsuit against his parents' neighbour, Antoinette Vento, the Township of Toms River, its Board of Adjustment and the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (DEP). In its opinion in David Faloba v. Antoinette Vento, available on LAWS.com, the court explained that the environmental agency had determined the pool complied with the applicable requirements, leaving no basis for the relief Faloba sought. The decision also addressed the limits of local authorities' powers and the proper legal route for challenging state agency action or inaction.Pool plans raised concerns over tidal floodingThe dispute began in 2024, when Vento applied to the Toms River Township Board of Adjustment for variances to construct an in-ground plunge pool on her residential property. The property sits on a barrier island beside a lagoon connected to Barnegat Bay, with a bulkhead separating the land from the water.An engineer representing Vento testified that the proposed pool would be 8.3 feet from her property's bulkhead. Although this distance complied with the relevant municipal setback requirement, it was less than the 15-foot setback generally specified under New Jersey's coastal development regulations. Faloba objected to the project, saying his parents' property experienced tidal flooding approximately once a month. He argued that the elevated pool could increase the flow of floodwater from Vento's property onto theirs.An engineer retained by Faloba also warned that the construction could worsen flooding and suggested changes to reduce the risk. Vento's attorney agreed that a retaining wall could be installed along the property boundary to help address the water flow. The Board of Adjustment granted the requested variances on May 23, 2024, subject to applicable approvals and requirements from other agencies. Faloba did not appeal that decision.Dispute centred on coastal construction regulationsA central question was whether Vento needed an individual environmental permit or could proceed under a permit-by-rule system. The rules applicable at the time allowed certain construction on waterfront lots with existing bulkheads, provided specified conditions were met.These conditions included demonstrating that there was no alternative to locating the proposed structure within 15 feet of the bulkhead, providing an engineering certification concerning future bulkhead replacement, and recording a conservation restriction. The rules have since been recodified. The regulation cited by Faloba, N.J.A.C. 7:7-4.22, concerned construction of pools and associated decking on bulkheaded lots without wetlands. The court explained that the relevant permit-by-rule requirements were subsequently moved to another section of the state regulations.Toms River issued a development permit for Vento's pool in July 2024 and a building permit the following month. Vento subsequently supplied the engineering certification and recorded a conservation restriction addressing future reconstruction of her bulkhead. Faloba continued to object, arguing that the permits had been issued before the environmental requirements were satisfied and that the project could not qualify under the applicable rules. He also alleged that the approvals infringed his parents' rights and amounted to a nuisance.Environmental agency found no violationThe DEP inspected the property in March 2025. Its records stated that the pool was eight feet from the bulkhead, that an engineering certification had been provided and that a conservation restriction had been recorded. The agency determined that the installation met the applicable permit-by-rule requirements for construction on a bulkheaded lagoon lot. It also found compliance with the relevant rules for construction in a tidal flood hazard area and recorded that no violation had been found.The DEP closed the matter on March 14, 2025. However, the agency's determination was not disclosed to the parties or the trial court at that time. Meanwhile, Faloba had filed a lawsuit seeking to invalidate the permits, halt construction and compel the authorities to enforce the environmental regulations. On April 25, 2025, the trial court dismissed the case with prejudice, rejecting his requests for relief, damages and legal costs.Appeals court upholds dismissalOn appeal, Faloba argued that the lower court had wrongly rejected his claims and that the authorities should have been compelled to enforce the law. The appellate court upheld the dismissal, finding that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to order the DEP to take the enforcement action he sought.The judges explained that challenges to state agency action or inaction must be brought through the appropriate appellate process. They also found that the DEP's determination that the pool complied with the relevant requirements had rendered the principal requests for relief moot. The court rejected the remaining claims as well, finding no basis to revive the civil rights and nuisance allegations. It therefore affirmed the dismissal of the lawsuit. The opinion was designated unpublished, meaning it is binding on the parties but generally cannot be cited as precedent in other cases under New Jersey's court rules. The ruling does not establish that waterfront pools can never worsen flooding or that every similar project automatically complies with coastal regulations. Instead, it underscores the importance of following the correct legal process and identifying the authority responsible for reviewing permits and enforcing environmental rules.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Tamil Nadu lawyer who once worked in a tea shop helped 30 tribal families secure long-delayed certificates in 2022, one young man later used the document to qualify for a government clerk's job
articles.summary: This is the story that proves humanity is still alive.
articles.body: This is the story that proves humanity is still alive. Meet advocate V Akathiyan who visited Vayaloor village in Tiruvannamalai district and helped nearly 30 tribal families belonging to the Kattunayakkan tribal community obtain their caste certificates which were long pending. Until the lawyer’s intervention, a piece of paper stood between a young man and his dream of securing a government job. For years, his family and other tribal households had approached government officials, submitting petitions in the hope of obtaining community certificates.The documents were important for getting educational opportunities and employment benefits.In 2022, Akathiyan came to the village and helped them. Among those who received the document was M Manikandan, a young man preparing for competitive examinations. Three years later, he cleared the examinations and secured a government clerk's job at the state secretariat.A childhood experience that shaped his missionAkathiyan's commitment to the cause began long before he became a lawyer. As a young boy, he saw a friend from a tribal community being denied school admission because he did not have a caste certificate. The incident left an impression on him. He educated himself about the topic and understood the importance of a piece of paper.Born in Royapuram, Chennai, Akathiyan grew up in Pillur in Villupuram district. His parents worked as daily-wage labourers. He completed his higher secondary education in Chidambaram while working at a tea shop. With financial support from well-wishers, he began studying law in 2013.Even as an undergraduate, he spent time visiting villages and understanding the issues faced by tribal communities. He eventually began practising at the Madras High Court in 2021.Why a community certificate can change a family's futureFor many people, a caste or community certificate is a routine administrative document. For members of Scheduled Tribe communities, however, it can determine whether they can access educational reservations, scholarships and employment.In Tamil Nadu, obtaining these certificates can be a challenging process, especially for families whose parents do not possess the necessary records.For families such as those in Vayaloor, the consequences are worse because without the needed paper, young people are at a higher risk of losing opportunities despite their willingness to study.Akathiyan's approach was to identify such families and understand their circumstances. He would then help them pursue the process with the relevant authorities. In the Vayaloor case, the results came quickly: all 30 families received their certificates within 15 days of his visit in 2022.From certificates to a government jobWhen Manikandan met Akathiyan in 2022, he was preparing for the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission's Group II examinations. He wanted to secure a government job, but he didn’t have a community certificate. The document was eventually issued along with those of the other families.Three years later, Manikandan cleared the examinations and secured a government clerk's position at the secretariat.Looking beyond paperworkAkathiyan's work has since extended to other tribal settlements, particularly in Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, Vellore and surrounding districts. Along with helping people secure community certificates, he has assisted some families in pursuing housing and other basic amenities. He also represents tribal people facing legal disputes and works to connect families with support for books, clothing and other essentials.But for Akathiyan, the task is not simply to help people obtain papers. It is also to ensure that eligible families can access opportunities and public services without being held back by prolonged administrative delays. Sometimes, opening a door does not require creating a new opportunity. It requires ensuring that someone who is already qualified to pursue it is finally allowed to walk through.You use AI every day. articles.body: At least 13 people were killed and 10 others injured after a Russian drone struck a platform at the railway station in Ukraine’s Dnipro on Thursday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.The attack took place on the Thursday morning, when a passenger train preparing to depart for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was standing at the platform. Ukraine’s state railway company, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a Russian jet-powered drone hit the platform where train No. 866, operating between Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia, was stationed.“Despite a warning of heightened danger, people were on the platform,” the railway company said in a statement on Telegram, adding that rescuers, medical personnel and law enforcement officers had reached the scene.Dnipro regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha confirmed that at least five people had been wounded, while Mayor Borys Filatov reported multiple fatalities and injuries. Zelenskyy later said the death toll had reached 13 and expressed condolences to the victims’ families.In a post on social media, Zelenskyy accused Russia of escalating its attacks on Ukraine and called on Western countries to tighten sanctions against Moscow.He questioned why Russia had continued launching strikes despite what he described as the easing of sanctions on certain Russian oligarchs and the country’s energy sector.“This is precisely why Ukraine has always said that just and decisive action by America and Europe is needed in response to Russian escalation,” Zelenskyy said, urging the European Union, the United States and the G7 to introduce stronger sanctions.Meanwhile, a Ukrainian delegation led by human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets has left for Russian-occupied Oleshky, where a ceasefire has reportedly been in place since Tuesday, senior Ukrainian official Davyd Arakhamia said. He added that the delegation would monitor the situation and provide updates when communication became available.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ex-Bangladesh air force officer linked to Hasina's fleeing clip found dead in Dhaka
articles.summary: A former Bangladesh Air Force officer, KM Tahsif Souri, was found dead in a river in Dhaka on Thursday, a day after he went missing.
articles.body: A former Bangladesh Air Force officer, KM Tahsif Souri, was found dead in a river in Dhaka on Thursday, a day after he went missing.According to the Daily Star, the 28-year-old had reportedly recorded a video showing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh on August 5, 2024,River police recovered Souri's body from the Tongi Bandar Ghat area after receiving a call through the national emergency helpline 999.The body was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for an autopsy. His identity was confirmed after his mobile phone and wristwatch were found with the body.According to Prothom Alo, Souri lived with his family in Sector 18 of Uttara.Police said the cause of death was not yet known. Although drowning was suspected, officials said the postmortem report would help establish the cause.Father says 'son felt unsafe'Souri's father KM Enayetul Karim Helal said he did not know who was responsible for his son's death. He told Jago News that Souri had sometimes expressed fears about his safety.“Tahsif would sometimes tell me that he was feeling a little apprehensive. But he never told me what he was worried about,” Helal said.According to his father, Souri was dismissed from the Air Force on disciplinary grounds. He later worked at the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB), Netra News and, most recently, Virgo Tobacco.“Before evening, one of his junior friends came to call him from downstairs. Tahsif told his mother, ‘Dip is here. I’ll go and talk to him.’ He went downstairs but never returned home,” he said.Video linked to Hasina's departureSouri's reported role in recording the video has drawn attention to his death. Hasina fled Dhaka on August 5, 2024, as mass protests led to the collapse of her government.She reportedly left by military helicopter before boarding a Bangladesh Air Force C-130J Hercules aircraft that flew to India's Hindon airbase in Ghaziabad.Hasina has remained in exile in India and has vowed to return to Bangladesh. However, police have not established any link between Souri's death and the video he reportedly recorded.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Wisconsin family commits $10 million to preserve a museum building famous for its giant moving wings overlooking Lake Michigan, ensuring the 25-year-old architectural landmark survives for future generations
articles.summary: A Wisconsin family has committed $10 million to preserve one of the most recognisable architectural landmarks on the shores of Lake Michigan, supporting
articles.body: A Wisconsin family has committed $10 million to preserve one of the most recognisable architectural landmarks on the shores of Lake Michigan, supporting the future of a museum building famous for its enormous moving wings. The Quadracci family’s contribution to the Milwaukee Art Museum will establish the Quadracci Pavilion Preservation Endowment Fund, which will finance the long-term care and maintenance of the structure’s defining architectural features. Announced on October 26, 2026, the commitment coincides with the pavilion’s 25th anniversary. Designed by Spanish-Swiss architect Santiago Calatrava, the building has become a symbol of Milwaukee’s identity, drawing attention for its striking white wings and distinctive design. The latest contribution brings the family’s total support for the museum to $30 million over three decades.How the $10 million fund will preserve the architectural landmarkThe contribution will establish an endowment dedicated to the pavilion’s ongoing care. Rather than funding a single announced renovation, the fund will generate annual income to support the maintenance of the building’s defining architectural features over the long term.The commitment comes from the Quadracci family, including Joel and Caran Quadracci, Dr Kathryn Quadracci Flores and Dr Raja Flores, Elizabeth Quadracci Harned and Chris Harned, as well as H. Richard Quadracci, who died in the summer of 2026. The Windhover and Winderful foundations are also involved in the initiative.The family’s latest contribution builds on its longstanding relationship with the museum. At the beginning of the pavilion project, Betty and Harry Quadracci provided a $10 million lead challenge grant. The family has since supported various museum projects and programmes, bringing its total contributions to $30 million over the past three decades.The giant moving wings that define Milwaukee’s skylineThe Quadracci Pavilion is best known for its Burke Brise Soleil, a large, wing-like structure that gives the building its distinctive silhouette. Its white movable wings extend over the museum’s entrance, creating a striking architectural feature visible along Milwaukee’s lakefront.Designed by Calatrava, the pavilion opened in 2001 and was his first building in the United States. Its design combines sculptural forms with engineering, making the structure a landmark in its own right rather than simply an entrance to the museum.The moving wings have become closely associated with Milwaukee’s skyline and civic identity. Beyond their visual appeal, the pavilion provides space for visitors to enter the museum, encounter its collections and take part in cultural activities. Its location beside Lake Michigan further connects the building’s design with the city’s waterfront.Why the family wants the pavilion to endureThe Quadracci family has described the commitment as a continuation of its parents’ vision for Milwaukee. Joel Quadracci said the original building project was only the first step, adding that its long-term care would help ensure it remained extraordinary for future generations.Kathryn Quadracci Flores said the pavilion represented the imagination and ambition associated with Milwaukee, while Elizabeth Quadracci Harned highlighted her parents’ belief that bringing people into contact with art could encourage creativity.The family’s contribution is intended to protect that legacy by supporting the pavilion’s defining features for years to come. The fund will also help the museum maintain a building that has become part of the city’s shared cultural experience, from family visits and school trips to community gatherings.Milwaukee Art Museum marks 25 years of the pavilionThe $10 million commitment coincides with the pavilion’s 25th anniversary. Since opening in 2001, the structure has become a defining part of the Milwaukee Art Museum’s 24-acre lakefront campus, which includes buildings designed by architects Santiago Calatrava, Eero Saarinen and David Kahler.The museum houses a collection of more than 35,000 works spanning different periods, regions and artistic traditions. Its activities include exhibitions and educational programmes that bring art to visitors of different ages and backgrounds.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Beyond US blockade: How Iran's secret 5,000+ agencies network keeps missiles flowing
articles.summary: Iran has continued importing materials that can be used to build missiles and drones despite Western sanctions and a US naval blockade, with a Reuters
articles.body: Iran has continued importing materials that can be used to build missiles and drones despite Western sanctions and a US naval blockade, with a Reuters investigation uncovering a network of thousands of agencies and overseas intermediaries involved in military procurement.The investigation found that one agency, identified as MOD 346428, imported military-related goods worth $2.3 billion between January 2025 and June 2026. The shipments included explosives, rocket-fuel ingredients, aircraft engine parts and heavy-duty trucks that can be modified to carry missile launchers.The findings offer insight into how Iran has continued acquiring supplies for its weapons programmes during the war, even as US and Israeli strikes have targeted its missile and drone capabilities.A hidden network of thousands of agenciesReuters identified more than 5,000 agencies with names beginning with MOD, followed by a five or six-digit number. The entities shared a registered address with Iran's Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics, known as MODAFL.The investigation, conducted with Israeli-American risk consultancy 240 Analytics, examined Iranian banking and government records, corporate filings and shipping data. It found that the agencies used foreign intermediaries and shell companies to purchase goods for Iran's military.The network's financial links also extended to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and businesses connected to Iran's political elite. Some of the agencies were linked to military personnel through records from Bank Sepah, an Iranian state-owned lender that handles salaries and pensions for the IRGC."What you have here is the regime's military lifeline during this conflict and for many years before," said Miad Maleki, a former senior US Treasury official who helped design American sanctions against Iran.How Iran moved money and military suppliesRather than relying on direct payments from Iran to foreign suppliers, the network used intermediaries who could pay for goods from overseas bank accounts. According to Reuters, 97% of the shipments it reviewed were settled "without currency transfer", making the transactions harder to trace through conventional cross-border payments.The goods reportedly entered Iran by several routes, including cargo ships across the Caspian Sea from Russia, trucks from Central Asia and freight aircraft from China. Import records also listed military-related goods originating in Germany and elsewhere in the European Union.The materials included chemicals used in rocket propellants, detonators, titanium and precision machinery. Such equipment can have civilian uses, but weapons experts who reviewed the findings said many of the items could support missile and drone production."This looks like an industrial-scale effort to rebuild or expand Iran's existing fleet" of drones and missiles, said Peter Salisbury, an adjunct assistant professor at Columbia University who researches Iranian arms transfers and supply chains.You use AI every day. articles.title: Karnataka hikes milk prices by Rs 8 per litre from Nov 1; farmers to get Rs 7 more
articles.summary: BENGALURU: The state Cabinet on Thursday decided to hike the Nandini milk base price by Rs 8 per litre. The hike will take effect from November 1.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The state Cabinet on Thursday decided to hike the Nandini milk base price by Rs 8 per litre. The hike will take effect from November 1.Citing the need to safeguard the interests of farmers reeling under severe drought, law and parliamentary affairs minister Krishna Byre Gowda justified the price hike, saying rates were still within the range of those in most other states.Tamil Nadu is the only state where the cooperative union milk rate is Rs 40 per litre.He said rising prices of other commodities were hurting farmers in the state and that milk supply had dropped by 10 lakh litres due to the drought this year.Cooperation minister Laxman Savadi said the government also had to consider the possibility of dairy farmers supplying milk to other states if rates were not hiked, potentially creating a milk shortage in Karnataka.Under the formula agreed upon, the government will ensure that Rs 7 of the increase goes to farmers and Re 1 goes to milk unions in the state."While farmers will get Rs 47 (including the Rs 5 given by the government as an incentive for milk production), the milk unions will get Re 1 per litre, keeping in mind the increase in transportation costs and packaging rates due to the rise in plastic prices," the two ministers said.When asked about the impact of the hike on consumers, Byre Gowda and Savadi said farmers, milk unions and legislators had sought an increase of Rs 10 per litre, but negotiations brought it down to Rs 8 to limit the burden on consumers.Byre Gowda said the government had to manage the expectations of dairy farmers, milk unions and consumers before arriving at the Rs 8-per-litre hike."Accordingly, the price of ghee, butter, cheese and other milk products will be hiked by the KMF," Savadi said.Comparative rates of base price of milkNandini- Current: Rs 46 per litre- From November 1: Rs 54 per litreOther articles.body: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman took a jibe at Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif over Field Marshal Asim Munir’s participation in a high-level regional security meeting in Iran, questioning why the defence minister was absent from the talks.According to a report by Dawn, Fazl raised the issue during his address to the National Assembly on Wednesday, referring to a meeting in Tehran attended by Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, alongside senior officials from Iran, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.“A defence pact is taking shape in Iran, a meeting is under way (there), and the defence minister is sitting here,” Fazl said, drawing laughter and desk-thumping in the House. He said the discussions had nothing to do with Pakistan’s defence or any related matter and argued that Munir had assumed a role focused on maintaining peace and dialogue following last year’s military conflict with India.The meeting brought together Munir, Naqvi, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, alongside senior Iranian officials, to discuss regional security and cooperation.A joint statement issued after the talks said the participants had agreed to continue their dialogue to strengthen cooperation among the four regional countries, particularly on peace and security.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also called for greater regional unity, saying closer cooperation among Muslim nations would help address shared challenges and resist external pressure.You use AI every day. articles.title: Karwa Chauth 2026: Moon Not Visible Tonight? Here’s How to Break Your Fast According to Hindu Traditions
articles.summary: A cloudy evening can turn Karwa Chauth into a long, anxious wait. Women who have gone without food and water since dawn keep stepping out to check the sky.
articles.body: A cloudy evening can turn Karwa Chauth into a long, anxious wait. Women who have gone without food and water since dawn keep stepping out to check the sky. Then they step back in. Today, Thursday, 29 October 2026, many will face exactly this. Haze, rain clouds or simple bad luck can hide the Moon well past its rising time.But the fast does not fail because of weather. Hindu tradition has worked out clear steps for such nights, and following them completes the vrat in full.Know Your Local Moonrise TimeKarwa Chauth is observed on the Chaturthi tithi of Kartik Krishna Paksha. The puja is usually done in the evening muhurat, roughly an hour or so before moonrise. Moonrise itself changes from place to place, sometimes by more than an hour. So check the exact time for your own city before evening.This time is the anchor for everything that follows. Chandra rises above the horizon at that minute, visible or not. The vrat is linked to the Moon’s rising, and a cloud in front of it does not cancel that event.Do Not RushThe most basic rule is simple. The fast must not end before the calculated moonrise. Family members may grow impatient. Some may insist the Moon is “surely up by now”. Still, wait for the clock.Once the rising time passes, give it a little longer. Most families wait 30 to 45 minutes. Clouds shift. A gap often opens for a few seconds, and that short glimpse is fully valid for the chalni ritual. Keep the thali, karwa and sieve close at hand so nothing is lost while fetching them.When the Moon Stays HiddenIf the sky does not clear, these customs are widely followed.Arghya towards the east. Face the direction where the Moon rises, which is broadly east. Fill the karwa with water and mix in a little raw milk, some rice grains and white flowers. Pour it in a slow, steady stream while praying to Chandra Dev. The offering is made to the Moon’s position, and faith carries it there.Moon darshan through Lord Shiva. Shiva wears the crescent Moon on his head. Because of this, seeing an image or idol of Shiva with the chandra through the sieve is accepted as darshan of the Moon. Many older women have used this method on overcast nights for decades.The Chandra mantra. Recite “Om Som Somaya Namah” 11 or 21 times during the arghya. In Vedic astrology, the Moon governs the mind and emotional peace. Chanting builds that link even when the planet cannot be seen.A prayer to Ganesha and Karwa Mata. Chaturthi is Lord Ganesha’s tithi. Bowing to him and to Karwa Mata before ending the fast is seen as essential, more so when the Moon does not appear.Never Use a Substitute MoonThe vrat katha has a lesson for exactly this moment. Queen Veervati was fainting from hunger, and her brothers could not watch. They placed a burning lamp behind a tree and convinced her it was the Moon. She ended her fast too early. Sorrow came to her household soon after.So a lamp raised high, a torch or a Moon photo on a phone should not stand in for Chandra. Video calls with relatives in places where the Moon is clearly out have become popular. Priests do not agree on whether this counts. Traditional families usually choose arghya and Shiva darshan instead.Ending the FastAfter the arghya, look at your husband’s face through the chalni. He gives the first sip of water and a small piece of sweet from the thali. Seek blessings from elders by touching their feet.Start eating slowly. A heavy meal right after hours without water can cause discomfort, so begin with something light like fruit or a little kheer.Women who are pregnant, diabetic or on daily medication should not push the wait to extremes. Scriptures place devotion above physical strain. And a calm, sincere prayer at the right time is what the ritual truly asks for.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates.
